questions.question_text: An irregular quadrilateral plot of land is divided by a diagonal of $18\text{ m}$. The perpendicular offsets on either side are $5\text{ m}$ and $8\text{ m}$. What is the area of the plot?

options.why: Forgot to halve the base times height when finding the triangle areas ($18 \times 5 + 18 \times 8$).
Calculated only the larger triangle area ($1/2 \times 18 \times 8$) and omitted the smaller triangle.
Multiplied the diagonal by the sum of offsets and divided by 4 instead of 2.
Calculated $26 \times (8 + 11)$ without dividing by 2 for the triangle areas.
Calculated only the lower triangle area ($1/2 \times 26 \times 11$) and omitted the top triangle.
Used the sum of offsets multiplied by the diagonal minus a triangle area.
Treated the central region as a rectangle of dimensions $16 \times 14\text{ m}$ instead of a trapezium.
Calculated only the central trapezium area and omitted the two end triangles.
Multiplied all base segments by heights without halving any of the triangular or trapezoidal areas.

questions.question_text: A commercial block of land is composed of a rectangle ($24\text{ m} \times 15\text{ m}$) and a triangular corner sharing the $24\text{ m}$ edge with a perpendicular height of $9\text{ m}$. What is the total area of the block?

options.why: Multiplied $24 \times 9$ without halving for the triangle area ($360 + 216$).
Calculated only the rectangular area and omitted the triangular corner.
Calculated only the triangular area and omitted the rectangle.

questions.question_text: An irregular quadrilateral field of total area $220\text{ m}^2$ has a diagonal of $20\text{ m}$. The perpendicular offset on one side of the diagonal is $6\text{ m}$. What is the length of the offset on the opposite side?

options.why: Found the sum of the offsets ($22\text{ m}$) but forgot to subtract the known offset of $6\text{ m}$.
Halved the correct answer twice by dividing by 2 an extra time.
Divided the remaining area ($160\text{ m}^2$) by the full diagonal length without multiplying by 2.

questions.question_text: A large paddock has a dividing diagonal of $150\text{ m}$ and perpendicular offsets of $40\text{ m}$ and $60\text{ m}$. What is its area in hectares ($1\text{ ha} = 10\,000\text{ m}^2$)?

options.why: Divided by $1000$ instead of $10\,000$ when converting square metres to hectares.
Calculated $150 \times (40 + 60) = 15\,000\text{ m}^2$ without halving for the triangles.
Calculated only the larger triangle area ($4500\text{ m}^2$) and converted to hectares.

questions.question_text: A triangular field is split along a baseline of $16\text{ m}$ (divided into $6\text{ m}$ and $10\text{ m}$) with a common perpendicular offset of $8\text{ m}$ at the division point. What is the perimeter of the field to the nearest metre?

options.why: Added the baseline and height ($16 + 8$) instead of finding the slanting boundary hypotenuses.
Rounded hypotenuse square roots prematurely before summing.
Added squared lengths rather than square roots when calculating perimeter.

questions.question_text: An irregular quadrilateral block $ABCD$ has a diagonal $AC = 28\text{ m}$ split into segments $12\text{ m}$ and $16\text{ m}$ by perpendicular offsets to $B$ ($9\text{ m}$) and $D$ ($12\text{ m}$). What is the perimeter of $ABCD$ to the nearest metre?

options.why: Added the diagonal and the two offsets twice rather than computing hypotenuses with Pythagoras.
Included the internal diagonal ($28\text{ m}$) in the outer perimeter sum.
Subtracted offset lengths from baseline segments before applying Pythagoras.

questions.question_text: An irregular quadrilateral paddock of total area $540\text{ m}^2$ has a diagonal of $36\text{ m}$. The perpendicular heights from the opposite vertices to the diagonal are in the ratio $2 : 3$. What is the length of the longer perpendicular height?

options.why: Found the shorter offset ($2 \times 6$) instead of the longer offset.
Found the sum of the two offsets ($30\text{ m}$) instead of the single longer offset.
Divided the sum of offsets ($30\text{ m}$) equally by 2 instead of using the ratio $2 : 3$.

questions.solution_text:
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times 36 \times (h_1 + h_2)$
$540 = 18(h_1 + h_2)$
$h_1 + h_2 = \frac{540}{18}$
$h_1 + h_2 = 30\text{ m}$
Total ratio parts $= 2 + 3 = 5$.
$\text{One part} = \frac{30}{5} = 6\text{ m}$
$\text{Longer offset} = 3 \times 6$
$= 18\text{ m}$
